artifacts.summary: All 8 phases completed: shared routing library, unified call sites, explicit routing_agents manifest declarations, single agent resolver adopted by both orchestrate engines, wiring-validation lint (gate7), table-driven parity test, skill-orchestrator retirement, and schema documentation.

completion_data.completion_summary: Consolidated six independent routing implementations onto one shared library (scripts/lib/manifest-routing-lib.sh) plus two thin resolvers (command-route-skill.sh refactored, command-route-agent.sh new); added explicit routing_agents/routing_agents_hard declarations across 17 manifests ground-truthed against each skill's own subagent_type dispatch; fixed implement.md's missing effort_flag argument; switched core-manifest identification to .name=="core"; retired skill-orchestrator; added lint-routing-wiring.sh (verify-deploy gate7) and an 18-assertion table-driven parity test. All 8 plan phases COMPLETED with zero unresolved deviations.

memory_candidates.content: When a shared bash library function needs to return TWO outputs to its caller (a value plus metadata like 'which precedence step matched'), do not use `$(function_call)` command substitution for the metadata side-channel — command substitution forks a subshell, so any non-local variable the function sets is invisible to the caller once the subshell exits. Under `set -u`, the caller's later reference to that now-unset variable is a hard error that silently kills the sourcing shell with zero output, which is very hard to diagnose (looks like the whole pipeline hung or produced nothing). Fix: have the function set both outputs as plain (non-subshelled) globals and have the caller invoke it directly (not via `$(...)`), reading both outputs immediately after the call — the same pattern used for constructs like SKILL_NAME/AGENT_NAME exports.

When a shared shell library must validate BOTH a deployed tree and its pre-deploy source store using the exact same resolution logic (e.g. a lint that should test what the live router actually does, not a re-derived copy), add a single environment-variable override for the manifest/data root (e.g. ROUTE_MANIFEST_ROOT) rather than parameterizing every function call. Default it to the value every live caller already uses, so behavior is provably unchanged (verify via a full before/after resolution-matrix diff); validation-only callers (lint, test) set the override to point at the source store instead. This lets one library serve both 'live behavior' and 'pre-deploy validation' consumers without duplicating logic.

When ground-truthing which agent a routing table's skill name actually dispatches to (rather than deriving it via string transformation, e.g. sed 's/^skill-//' + '-agent'), grep each candidate skill's SKILL.md for its literal `subagent_type:`/`subagent_type =` dispatch line rather than trusting the skill-name-to-agent-name naming convention to hold universally. In a real manifest set, roughly 15-20% of entries broke a naive derivation (compound multi-stage skills that pick an agent dynamically at runtime, skills whose agent name doesn't follow the skill-name pattern, skills that are direct-execution with no agent at all). A cross-check against provides.agents alone is not sufficient either — a manifest's routing.{op} value can point to a DIFFERENT skill than the one whose agent name superficially matches the task_type (e.g. a 'document' sub-key routing to the SAME generic skill/agent as the parent key, not a document-specific one).
